questions.question: Which of the following defines the fundamental structural and functional unit of the body?
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

questions.question: The dense central part of the protoplasm is known as which structure?
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the central, denser portion of the protoplasm enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

questions.question: The fluid base of the cytoplasm is referred to as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The cytosol or hyaloplasm is the fluid matrix of the cytoplasm that contains organelles.

questions.question: Membrane-bound spaces within the cytosol are collectively called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The spaces enclosed by organelle membranes within the cytosol are collectively termed the vacuoplasm.

questions.question: The membrane separating the cytoplasm from surrounding structures is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane or plasma membrane separates the cytoplasm from the surrounding environment.

questions.question: The cell membrane regulates entry and exit of compounds through which property?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane has highly selective permeability that regulates the passage of compounds.

questions.question: The average thickness of a cell membrane as seen under an electron microscope is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is approximately 7.5 nm thick under the electron microscope.

questions.question: The trilaminar appearance of the cell membrane consists of which arrangement?
options: One dense and one light layer
Two light layers with a dense zone
Two dense layers with a light zone
questions.explanation: The membrane shows two densely stained layers separated by a lighter zone.

questions.question: Membranes are mainly made up of which combination of substances?
questions.explanation: Membranes consist mainly of lipids, proteins, and small amounts of carbohydrates.

questions.question: The basic framework of the cell membrane is constituted by which molecules?
questions.explanation: Phospholipids predominantly constitute the basic framework of membranes.

questions.question: The water-soluble end of a phospholipid molecule is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The head end containing phosphate is soluble in water and is called the polar end.

questions.question: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed by which scientists?
questions.explanation: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model of membrane structure in 1972.

questions.question: Phospholipids in an aqueous medium arrange themselves into which structure?
questions.explanation: Phospholipids form a bi-layer with hydrophilic heads facing the aqueous medium.

questions.question: The dark staining parts of the membrane seen by EM are formed by which component?
questions.explanation: The heads of phospholipid molecules form the dark staining parts of the membrane.

questions.question: Because of its manner of formation, the cell membrane is best regarded as which type of structure?
questions.explanation: The membrane is a fluid structure that can readily reform when disturbed.

questions.question: Which lipid provides stability to the cell membrane?
questions.explanation: Cholesterol is present in membranes and provides stability to them.

questions.question: Which glycolipid is an important constituent of myelin?
questions.explanation: Galactocerebroside is a glycolipid and an important constituent of myelin.

questions.question: Glycolipids are present in which location of cell membranes?
questions.explanation: Glycolipids are present only over the outer surface of cell membranes.

questions.question: Proteins occupying the entire thickness of the membrane and projecting from both surfaces are called which of the following?
questions.explanation: Transmembrane proteins span the full thickness and project out of both membrane surfaces.

questions.question: Membrane proteins that form passive channels allow substances to pass through which process?
questions.explanation: Passive channels allow substances to diffuse through the membrane.

questions.question: Proteins that bind specific hormones or neurotransmitters act as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Receptor proteins are specific for particular molecules like hormones or neurotransmitters.

questions.question: Proteins play a vital role in transport across the membrane by acting as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Some proteins act as pumps that carry ions from one surface to the other.

questions.question: Carbohydrates attached to proteins on the membrane form which structure?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates attached to proteins form glycoproteins.

questions.question: The carbohydrate layer on the external surface of the plasma membrane is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: The well-developed carbohydrate layer on the external surface is called the glycocalyx.

questions.question: The cell membrane maintains which property of the cell?
questions.explanation: One of the primary functions of the cell membrane is maintaining the shape of the cell.

questions.question: The plasma membranes of nerve and muscle cells are normally polarised with which charge distribution?
questions.explanation: The external surface bears a positive charge and the internal surface a negative charge.

questions.question: The potential difference across a polarised nerve cell membrane may be as much as which value?
questions.explanation: The potential difference across polarised nerve and muscle cell membranes may be as much as 100 mv.

questions.question: Reversal of the charge across a membrane upon stimulation is called which of the following?
questions.explanation: Selective passage of sodium and potassium ions reversing the charge is called depolarisation.

questions.question: Depolarisation of a muscle cell membrane results in which outcome?
questions.explanation: Depolarisation results in contraction in the case of muscle cells.

questions.question: The membranes of rod and cone cells of the retina bear proteins sensitive to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Rod and cone cell membranes bear proteins that are sensitive to light.
